derivation: Foundation 48 GameWindow. Read from the pinned Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game.dll IL. GameWindow is `.class public abstract auto ansi beforefieldinit` extending System.Object, with twenty selected identities: eleven methods, six properties and three events. It declares six private EventHandler`1 fields -- Activated, Deactivated, Paint, ScreenDeviceNameChanged, ClientSizeChanged, OrientationChanged -- but the add/remove accessors of the first three are `assembly`, so only the last three are identities. Ten members are abstract for a concrete host to supply: get_Handle, get_AllowUserResizing, set_AllowUserResizing, get_ClientBounds, get_ScreenDeviceName, get_CurrentOrientation, BeginScreenDeviceChange(bool), the three-argument EndScreenDeviceChange, the family SetTitle(string) and the famorassem SetSupportedOrientations(DisplayOrientation). get_Title is one ldfld and set_Title throws ArgumentNullException("value", Resources.TitleCannotBeNull) on null, compares with String::op_Inequality and only then writes the field and calls the abstract SetTitle, so a same-value write pushes nothing. The abstract constructor is `assembly` and sets title = String.Empty, but WindowsGameWindow's constructor calls base..ctor() and then set_Title(GetDefaultTitleName()), so the value a consumer observes before writing one is the host's default rather than the empty string. The one-argument EndScreenDeviceChange is concrete and thirty bytes: EndScreenDeviceChange(name, ClientBounds.Width, ClientBounds.Height). The six family On* raisers are each twenty-six bytes, `if (X != null) X(this, EventArgs.Empty)`. Game::get_Window is `host?.Window`, and its null branch is unreachable in XNA because Game..ctor calls EnsureHost().
